review_notes: I read the whole file. The two compactness arguments are parallel: one shows a projection hits the eventual range, the other lifts an element along a pointwise-surjective map. They repeat the same machinery in different places. I compared both blocks line by line. I did not check the proposed generalizations against Lean, and the cast-based predicate for the sections case may need adjusting. The empty-index branch of `limit_map_surjective` repeats the body of `limit_element_ext`. That is a short snippet, so I did not report it. I also checked that the cofiltered-system API (`IsCofiltered.inf`, `infTo`) is used in the same way in both blocks.

findings.problem: The two directedness proofs are the same argument. Both build the embeddings ιA and ιB, take the union diagram C, and prove that every arrow of A or B lies in C.arrows. Both then restrict the solution via `simpa [ιA] using hs hf'`. The only difference is the object-wise condition (`s j = x` against the η-fibre condition). That condition is passed through as `hsj` in one proof and as `fun k hk ↦ hsη k (Finset.mem_union_left _ hk)` in the other. The 30-line block is duplicated verbatim at lines 323–356. A change to `PointedFiniteDiagram` or `FiniteDiagramArrow` has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove one lemma that is generic in the object-wise condition. Let `Q : ∀ k, F.obj k → Prop` and set `partialSections Q D := {s | (∀ k ∈ D.objects, Q k (s k)) ∧ ∀ {f} (_ : f ∈ D.arrows), F.map f.2.2.2.2 (s f.1) = s f.2.1}`. Prove `Directed GE.ge (partialSections Q)` once, using the ιA/ιB/C construction. Membership in the union gives `Q` on the smaller object set by monotonicity.

For the lifts case take `Q k y := η.app k y = limit.π G k t`. For the sections case take `Q k y := ∀ h : k = j, h ▸ y = x`. Since `j ∈ D.objects` always, this is equivalent to `s j = x`. Alternatively keep `s j = x` as a separate conjunct and parametrise by an extra predicate on `s`. Then `partialSectionsAt_directed` and `partialLiftsAt_directed` become one-line specialisations, or are replaced by the generic lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes about 30 duplicated lines of fiddly Finset/Sigma bookkeeping and keeps the structural argument in one place. A reader sees that directedness does not depend on the particular condition, so the proof is easier to check and maintain.

findings.proposed_change:
With the generic `partialSections Q D` above, prove once `partialSections_closed (hQ : ∀ k, IsClosed {y : F.obj k | Q k y}) D : IsClosed (partialSections Q D)`. The proof writes the set as `(⋂ k ∈ D.objects, {s | Q k (s k)}) ∩ ⋂ f ∈ D.arrows, {s | F.map … = s f.2.1}`. The first part is closed by `isClosed_biInter` and `(hQ k).preimage (continuous_apply k)`. The second is closed by the existing `isClosed_eq <;> fun_prop` argument.

The lifts case supplies `hQ k` as the existing `isClosed_eq ((η.app k).hom.continuous …) continuous_const`. The sections case supplies the closedness of `{s j = x}` (or of the cast-defined set).
findings.benefit: The topological argument, which is the only place compact Hausdorff structure is used, appears once. The two uses then differ only in the closed condition they supply.

findings.problem:
The two existence theorems repeat the same compactness argument. Both start from the singleton diagram to get `Nonempty (PointedFiniteDiagram j)`. Both apply `IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed` to the family of closed sets. Both then show that the resulting point is a compatible tuple by evaluating `Set.mem_iInter.mp hs D` at the diagram `{j,X,Y}` with the single arrow `f` (lines 215–219 and 398–403).

The nonemptiness proofs (lines 121–138 and 294–321) repeat the same cofiltered construction. Both take `infTo`, push a chosen `y : F.obj (inf …)` forward along `F.map (infTo …)` on `D.objects` and use 0 elsewhere. Both prove arrow compatibility with the identical `rwa [dite_eq_left hX, dite_eq_left hY, ← comp_apply, ← F.map_comp, @IsCofiltered.infTo_commutes …]`. This is nontrivial reasoning, and it is duplicated rather than shared.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma. Given `Q` as above with closed fibres, and a hypothesis `hQ : ∀ D : PointedFiniteDiagram j, ∃ y : F.obj (IsCofiltered.inf D.objects D.arrows), ∀ i (hi : i ∈ D.objects), Q i (F.map (IsCofiltered.infTo D.objects D.arrows hi) y)`, conclude `∃ s : (limitCone F).pt, ∀ k, Q k (s.1 k)`. The proof does three things:

1. Build the section from `y` as in the current `…_nonempty` proofs, using the shared `dite_eq_left … infTo_commutes` argument for compatibility.
2. Apply `IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed` with the generic directed and closed lemmas.
3. Extract compatibility from the `{j,X,Y}` diagram and `Q` from the `{j,k}` diagram.

The sections case discharges `hQ` from `mem_eventualRange_iff` at `infTo D.objects D.arrows D.point_mem`. The lifts case discharges it with `hη (inf …)`, then naturality and `limit.w`, which is the existing `calc` at lines 313–317.

`exists_limitCone_point_of_mem_eventualRange` and `exists_limitCone_lift` become short wrappers that supply `Q` and `hQ`.
findings.benefit: The shared lemma holds the cofiltered/compactness argument once, so it can be read and maintained in one place. Only the genuinely different mathematics stays in the wrappers: the eventual-range hypothesis in one, and the naturality/limit-compatibility calculation in the other. This cuts about 100 lines of near-copy and reduces the chance of the two proofs drifting apart.
